For renamed kits, create.mjs rewrites the kit specifier relative to each destination file. The kit index exports Presentation, Appear, Box, SceneLayer and the types SceneProps and Step. Prop and field checks: Talk.tsx passes className, steps, title and initialMode, all in PresentationProps, and brand and attribution are optional. Steps carry id, era, title, caption, Scene, groupKey and payload, matching Step and StepMeta. Appear takes HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, so style is valid and key is React's own. Box takes the required id plus kind and style. SceneLayer takes HTMLAttributes. The inspect template (bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs) only imports './lib.mjs', playwright and node built-ins, and it lands in scripts/ next to lib.mjs. The build script is 'tsc -b && vite build', and tsconfig.app.json includes src with types vite/client, so the CSS import type-checks. The tsconfig flags are noUnusedLocals, verbatimModuleSyntax and erasableSyntaxOnly. The templates use 'import type' for types and have no unused locals. Test evidence: tests/verify.e2e.test.ts ('verifies a project whose kit and registry were renamed, using a presentation made by create.mjs') scaffolds a project, renames the kit and registry, runs create.mjs, and runs scripts/verify.mjs. It expects VERIFY PASSED, which includes the build. I did not run this test.

votes.rationale: Talk and the shared Scene use the kit's public API and do not re-implement it. Talk renders the kit's Presentation with steps, title, className and initialMode. Every step is a kit Step with Scene, groupKey and payload. The shared SampleScene builds its diagram only from kit primitives: SceneLayer, Appear, Box, SymbolChip, Arrow, Emphasis, Label and Frame. votes.rationale: Grouping: every one of the nine steps is produced by one BEATS.map in steps/index.ts with groupKey 'scene' and Scene SampleScene. Stage.tsx computes sceneKey = step.groupKey ?? step.id and uses it as the key of the single motion.div. The key is therefore the same across all nine steps, so navigating changes only the payload and the scene instance is not remounted. Identity is separate. entities.ts defines the presentation-owned ID constants with htm/-namespaced strings. Scene.tsx passes each as id={ID.x}, and the kit primitives forward that id to entityProps as layoutId. Because layout: true is set too, an entity present in consecutive steps morphs in place. Every ID member is consumed by a rendered element in Scene.tsx: you, prompt, skill, converse, question, tray, card1-3, link1, link2, morph1, morph2, ghost, depth, socket, plug, verify, verifyLink, pass, modify, modifyLabel, flag, frame and frameLabel. That includes the arrow connectors, so none is dead. Each Placed wrapper has a stable key, so AnimatePresence does not remount entities across steps. The geometry-changing entities, tray and link1, keep the same ID with new size values.

votes.rationale: Active chrome: Toc.tsx puts aria-current='step' and data-active on the TOC buttons. Footer.tsx does the same on the progress dots. talk.css styles those hooks. The TOC entry with data-active='true' gets a gold color, a gold left border, a tinted background and bold weight. The active progress dot gets a filled gold background and a 1.5x scale. Both are visibly distinct from the inactive state. Attribution: Presentation.tsx renders a project-local anchor with data-presentation-attribution, using ATTRIBUTION_HREF and ATTRIBUTION_LABEL from the local constants.ts. There is no external package or remote embed. talk.css makes it legible with an explicit font size, a muted color on the dark panel, an underline with offset, and a gold hover. Talk.tsx imports talk.css. Kit free of defaults: I searched all of src/presentation-kit for color, font, border, background, hex/rgb/hsl, var(--, shadow, fill, stroke, filter, gradient, outline, cursor, radius, className, style and CSS imports. The only inline styles are structural layout (position, flex/grid, size, transform, overflow) in Stage.tsx, Presentation.tsx, Stacked.tsx and SceneLayer.tsx. The only animated property is opacity, in Stage.tsx and Appear.tsx. That is motion behavior, not a theme token. constants.ts holds only timing, geometry and attribution link values, with no colors or fonts. Header, Toc, Footer, Emphasis and SymbolChip emit data-* hooks only. The comments in Box, Frame and Arrow say the same: hooks only, no visual defaults, arrow heads drawn by presentation CSS. The kit imports no CSS file. The only CSS imports in src are talk.css (Talk.tsx) and index.css (main.tsx). So colors, fonts, borders and button styles live in presentation-owned CSS and the reusable kit stays unstyled.

checks.rationale: The cited material shows what the dissent claims. When the canonical sample's steps content is absent (STEPS empty), the build passes and checkRegistered passes, because the registry entry and the Talk module still exist. The step-count and title/caption comparisons that would report phase=sample run only after the selector appears, so they are never reached. The review guidance includes 'steps content (titles, captions, steps) is absent' in the definition of a missing sample. It says a failure that surfaces only as a render timeout does not name the failed phase and fails the criterion. The verifier also has no title/caption check before rendering. The majority's point about unregistered and out-of-order samples is accurate but does not cover this case. The decider's 'partial-deletion' objection does not apply: the guidance's example of partial deletion is removing an imported file while its import remains, not emptying the steps content, which the guidance names explicitly. tests/verify.e2e.test.ts has no fault for absent step content.

result.rationale: The requirement is met: when the reference sample is missing, verification exits non-zero and its output names the sample phase. In scripts/verify.mjs, main() runs the build and then calls checkRegistered(slug) for the canonical sample before any browser work. If the registry has no entry for the slug, checkRegistered throws Failure('sample', '... is not registered ...'). If the entry's imported module does not exist, it throws a sample-phase Failure saying so. The top-level handler prints 'VERIFY FAILED phase=sample' and calls process.exit(1). The outline is also checked in phase=sample. If the step count differs from the nine CANONICAL steps, that is a sample-phase Failure. If any step's title or caption differs from CANONICAL in order, that is a sample-phase Failure naming the step. tests/verify.e2e.test.ts runs verify.mjs on modified throwaway copies of the repo and asserts a non-zero exit plus the matching message. The faults cover an unregistered sample, a sample directory deleted and replaced by another reference, and out-of-order steps. Judge B argued that absent step content only produces a generic render timeout. That depends on emptying the steps array to zero entries, which is a constructed partial-deletion case. The guidance says not to construct those, and it credits a verifier that fails a missing sample with an explicit check reporting it as missing or not matching the outline, which this verifier has. Any steps that are removed, reordered, or retitled while the deck still renders hit the sample-phase count or title/caption checks. So B's reason does not decide the requirement, and I rule pass as judges A and C did.

verification-tooling.rationale: The port comes from freePort(), which closes its probe server before vite starts. Readiness is HTTP polling of that port, with `if (exited) break` sampled only before each fetch. The child's stdout is never parsed for a listening announcement, and its exit is not raced against the fetch.
